### `pilecap.testing.COOLDOWN_KEY`

The cache key that says "do not call the primary". Short-lived on purpose: it is the whole of the cooldown, and its expiry IS the re-probe.

- value · source `apps/search/selectors.py:192`
- golden: `search`

### `pilecap.testing.DEGRADED_KEY`

The cache key that says "we have announced a degradation and not yet announced a recovery". It has **no expiry**, deliberately: the cooldown key expiring every few seconds must not be mistaken for the outage ending, and a flag that timed out on its own would announce the same degradation again on the next failure — a pair that can be raised twice and lowered once. Its whole life is one atomic `add` (the claim to announce degraded) and one atomic `delete` (the claim to announce recovered).

- value · source `apps/search/selectors.py:201`
- golden: `search`

### `pilecap.testing.REQUEST_FIXED_QUERIES`

**What any authenticated, tenant-resolved REST request pays before its own read** — the one fixed cost every door test in the tree can import instead of re-measuring it. Measured on this tree's organizations, memberships and invitations lists (each 8 statements, of which the page is one) and itemised once, so a change to it is a change to one of these and says which: the session row and the user row (Django's session and auth middleware); the membership read that resolves the tenant and the one that resolves the hat (`core.middleware`); and, with no request transaction (ADR perf-2), the three reads `<kind>.read` costs at the hat — the memberships on the chain, their grants, and the delta rows for the role keys they name (paid once per actor, `authz`'s memo). A product's list pin is this plus its own reads.

- value · source `apps/core/tests/wire.py:63`
- golden: `adopt.archive`, `adopt.attach`, `adopt.bulk`, `adopt.duplicate`, `adopt.history`, `adopt.import`, `adopt.merge`, `adopt.move`, `adopt.version`, `noun`, `portal`

### `pilecap.testing.TEXT_SEARCH_CONFIG`

The Postgres text-search configuration both halves of the fallback use — the `to_tsvector` config for the corpus and the `to_tsquery` config for the query. **They have to be the same one**: a vector built under `english` and a query parsed under `simple` disagree about stemming and stop words, and the failure is a search that quietly finds less rather than an error anybody sees.

- value · source `apps/search/selectors.py:176`
- golden: `search`

### `pilecap.testing.VECTOR_FIELD`

The column an adopting model declares. When a model has it, the fallback reads it and Postgres can use the GIN index over it; when it does not, the same vector is computed from the same declared fields on the fly — the same tsquery and the same ranking function with a sequential scan under it instead of an index. **Correct either way, fast only the first way**, and that asymmetry is stated rather than hidden. `apps/example/models.py`'s `Widget.search_vector` is the worked adopting column and the first member of the declaring population, so both branches now have a model in the tree — `tests/test_degradation.py` drives the computed one and `apps/example/tests/test_search_adoption.py` drives the real one.

- value · source `apps/search/selectors.py:188`
- golden: `search`
